paper_metadata.title: Semi-solid brazing via CoCrFeNiCux high-entropy alloy fillers: interfacial microstructure, mechanical properties, and joining mechanism of C/C-SiC composites and TZM alloy

evidence.quote: This study proposes a semi-solid brazing strategy, which uses CoCrFeNiCu x high-entropy alloy filler to connect C/C-SiC composites with TZM (titanium-zirconium-molybdenum alloy).
The metallic substrate employed is a rolled TZM alloy (Titanium-Zirconium-Molybdenum Alloy)
this study designed a series of high-entropy alloy fillers of CoCrFeNiCux (x = 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0) with different Cu contents

When CoCrFeNiCu4.0 filler is used for brazing, no obvious brazing defects are observed at the interface, and almost complete connection between filler and composites is realized.
The C/C-SiC composite material used in this investigation, depicted in Fig. 1(a), was fabricated by a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) process.
The metallic substrate employed is a rolled TZM alloy (Titanium-Zirconium-Molybdenum Alloy), with its microstructure and XRD profile depicted in Figs. 1(c)(d).

evidence.quote: at 1000 °C, the shear strength declines markedly to 29.31 MPa. At this extreme temperature, the filler alloy undergoes excessive softening and its fracture strength drops to a minimum (Fig. 19(b)), leading to the loss of structural load-bearing capacity and subsequent interfacial failure.
